s: A cosy clockwork idle climber about a hive of wind-up insects, a stopped tower and one very helpful moth made of light.
x: The stopped tower: amber honeycomb windows, brass girders and a moth of living light. Deep inside a clock tower whose great mainspring ran down long ago, a hive of tiny clockwork insects is waking up. The Rust has crept over every floor. Hivewright is an idle and incremental game for Android. You gather by hand, build homes, wake wind-ups and give each one a job. Soon the hive runs itself, even while the phone is in your pocket. Then you send swarms up the tower, floor by floor, past the Rust and the Gatekeepers that guard each level, towards the heart of the clock. The hook A hive that works while you are away. Your wind-ups keep gathering, and the swarm keeps climbing, when you close the game. A welcome-back summary shows what the hive earned. A tower with no top. Every hundred floors a great clock is restarted, and the tower keeps rising. Rewind. From floor 20 you can wind time back, start the hive again and keep permanent perks, so every run climbs further than the last. A key that matters. The hive's great key slowly unwinds. A wound hive works and fights harder, so tapping still has a point long after the first minutes. No account, no internet needed. Play offline, at your own pace. How a session feels A short visit is a handful of taps, a few new wind-ups, a quick check on the climb and a decision about what to spend. You might wind the key, build a Cell, study a new schematic or pick one of three Salvage finds after a Gatekeeper falls. A long visit is more of a plan: which perks to buy before the next Rewind , which Trial to try, which side chamber might hold the next equipment pattern. The hive teaches you as you go. The lantern moth suggests one goal at a time and moves on by itself when you meet it, which is how the first ten minutes go. The world The windows are honeycomb and glow amber. The music is a soft music-box melody with ticking in the background, and it gains layers as the hive grows. The wind-ups themselves change as you equip them. A newly made beetle is plain brass; later it grows mandibles and a stinger, armour, glass-and-brass wings and, much later, a veteran's harness. See Equipment and expeditions for how each look arrives. The moth A lantern moth made of living light lives with the hive from the first minute. It flits to whichever part of the hive is busiest, and its light makes that work go faster. It chooses where it goes, not you, and it glows brighter every time a great clock restarts. It cannot be bought, fed or upgraded. More on the lantern moth . Where to go next If you want to... Everything else sticks to what the early screens already show. Hivewright is made by BlairsLab. It is available

s: Your first ten minutes in the hive, step by step, following the lantern moth's goals.
x: Home Hivewright Start here Getting started Getting started Your first ten minutes in the hive, step by step, following the lantern moth's goals. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The screen The moth's first goals What to do while the moth is quiet After floor 1 When you open Hivewright for the first time you see three short welcome pages (the stopped tower, your hive, the lantern moth) and then the hive itself. The hive starts with no homes and no wind-ups. The Jobs tab: tap a resource to gather it, then give wind-ups jobs with the + and - buttons. The screen The bottom bar has six tabs: Jobs, Build, Research, Climb, Journal and Rewind . Not all of them are useful at once; several wake up as you progress. Across the top you see your stock of Oil , Brass , Springs and Schematics , with the limit of each store and how much is arriving every second. The moth's first goals The lantern moth gives you one goal at a time and moves to the next by itself when you meet it. The opening goals are: Build your first Cell. In the Jobs tab, tap Brass until you have 10, then build a Cell in the Build tab. Wind-ups need somewhere to live, and the hive starts with no room. Wake your first wind-up. Tap Oil in the Jobs tab. The Hatchery uses a little Oil to assemble each wind-up. Give it a job. Tap + beside Oilers or Braziers. Workers gather by themselves, even while you are away. Grow the hive to 8 wind-ups. Build more Cells and keep Oil coming for the Hatchery. Research Coil Winding. Tap Schematics in the Jobs tab, then study Coil Winding in the Research tab. It discovers Springs. Hire a Coiler to gather Springs for you. Research the Draughting Table and give a wind-up the Draughtsman job, so Schematics arrive without tapping. Research Swarm Drill. This opens the Climb tab, and the great key begins to unwind. Equip a swarm and start climbing. In the Climb tab, level Mandibles and Shells with Springs, then tap Start climbing . Clear floor 1. Beat the Gatekeeper on the 50th cog. Upgrade your equipment if swarms keep falling. Tip The first wind-ups arrive fast. Until the hive holds eight wind-ups, the Hatchery works much quicker than normal. What to do while the moth is quiet Tap early, delegate soon. Tapping gathers one resource at a time and is worth doing at the start. As soon as a wind-up has a job, you are earning for free. Watch the limits. Each store has a limit. When Oil, Brass or Springs reach it, gathering stops. Build an Oil Cistern, Brass Bin or Spring Rack to raise it. See Build and research . Keep housing ahead of the Hatchery. The Hatchery needs room. A line saying the hive is full means you need more Cells. After floor 1 The next goals are to keep the great key wound (tap Wind , or give about one wind-up in ten the Winder job), reach floor 10 for your first Salvage and for expeditions, and reach floor 20 for your first Rewind . Full details are on The great key and How the climb works . Note Clearing floors 5 and 15 for the first time in your hive's first run gives a half hour of Lantern Glow as a gift: a spell of doubled gathering and hatching. Floor 10 brings your first story page. Next, read How the climb works , or go to Tips for fast progress . Next How the climb works

s: Floors, cogs, swarms and Swarmers: how your wind-ups fight their way up the tower.
x: Home Hivewright Guides How the climb works How the climb works Floors, cogs, swarms and Swarmers: how your wind-ups fight their way up the tower. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page Floors and cogs Swarms and Swarmers Strength What a floor pays The way back up Reading a stall The Climb tab opens when you research Swarm Drill . From then on your hive can send swarms of wind-ups up the tower against the Rust. The Climb tab: your current floor, the cog you are on, and the wind-ups' current look. Floors and cogs The tower is made of floors . Each floor has 50 cogs , and each cog holds one enemy. Your swarm fights the Rust creatures one cog at a time. The enemy on the last cog of a floor is the Gatekeeper , which is tougher than anything before it. Beat it and you move up a floor, and the floor pays out supplies. Every tenth floor is a landmark floor . Its Gatekeeper leaves behind a story fragment and a choice of Salvage . Swarms and Swarmers Every swarm is made from the Swarmer job, not from idle wind-ups. While you are climbing, idle and new wind-ups fill the Swarmer reserve first, up to one swarm. A swarm starts at 5 wind-ups . Each level of Formation Drills research makes swarms 25% larger (compounding). A swarm can never be more than half your housing , so a big swarm needs a big hive. Stop climbing calls the swarm home at once. Survivors rejoin the Swarmers if the hive has room. If a swarm falls, a new one assembles from the Swarmers, and the floor you reached is kept. Assembly speed matters: the Hatchery and Hatchery Tuning make a fallen swarm return sooner. Strength A single wind-up starts with 1 attack and 10 health. Equipment adds to those numbers, and then everything is multiplied together: the Tuner job (+1% swarm attack and health each), the Proving Ground building (+10% each), perks bought with Aether, the great key's tension , which scales attack from 75% to 100% in normal play, the lantern moth, when it has settled on the swarm, curios, Loft trains and Salvage choices. Swarms strike at a steady rhythm. Each Escapement Hall you build makes swarms strike 3% more often. What a floor pays Clearing a floor pays supplies equal to about a minute of your hive's gathering , with a minimum of 15 times the floor number. Gatekeepers and the Rust on every tenth cog also drop Gearshards , the currency for expeditions . The way back up If you Rewind, you climb again from floor 1. Floors more than ten below your best in the current Era are remembered : the Rust there is weaker the further down it is, and a strike that overkills one creature carries on into the next. That is why the early floors fly by after a Rewind. Tip When a swarm keeps falling on the same floor, level your weakest piece of equipment, wind the key, build a Proving Ground, or look for a new Salvage choice. The game also offers an optional boost after a few falls on the same level; see Offline progress and optional boosts . Reading a stall Hitting a wall is normal; the tower scales faster than a single run's growth. The usual cures are: Spend Springs on equipment. Make sure the great key is wound. Research Formation Drills. Rewind for Aether and buy perks. See Rewind and perks . For the numbers behind each floor, see Floors and Rust . s: How wind-ups are made, what each job does, and why keeping the great key wound matters.
x: Home Hivewright Guides Wind-ups, jobs and the great key Wind-ups, jobs and the great key How wind-ups are made, what each job does, and why keeping the great key wound matters. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page Making wind-ups Jobs The great key and Tension Tapping Helpers A newly made wind-up: plain, smooth brass, with a key on its back. Wind-ups do the gathering and the fighting, and you get more of them as you build homes. Making wind-ups You need housing first. A Cell houses 3 wind-ups, a Comb 7, a Gallery 18 and, later on, a Spire 35. See Build and research . The Hatchery assembles a new wind-up about every 20 seconds while there is room, using 6 Oil each. Build more Hatcheries to go faster. Hatchery Tuning research adds 20% assembly speed per level. Idle wind-ups also help: each one adds 2% to the Hatchery's pace. Until the hive holds 8 wind-ups, assembly runs much faster than normal, so the first minutes are quick. Jobs Open the Jobs tab to assign wind-ups. The move buttons (x1, x10, All) change how many move at once. Each job appears when its research is done. Job What it does Needs Oiler Gathers 0.5 Oil per second Nothing Brazier Gathers 0.4 Brass per second Nothing Coiler Gathers 0.3 Springs per second Coil Winding research Draughtsman Draws 0.2 Schematics per second Draughting Table research Tuner Trains swarms: +1% swarm attack and health each Swarm Drill, and floor 2 Winder Keeps the great key wound Swarm Drill Swarmer Waits ready for battle; every swarm is made from Swarmers Swarm Drill Those rates are per wind-up before any bonus. Research, the Offering Altar, perks, the moth and the Lantern Glow all multiply them. Tip Gearshards cannot be gathered by a job. They only drop from Gatekeepers and the Rust. The great key and Tension Every wind-up runs on its spring, and the hive has one great key. The key slowly unwinds , and the hive's Tension meter shows how wound it is: Work and attack run at 50% plus half of the Tension . Fully wound is 100%. The key unwinds by about 1% every six seconds, but never below half wound . That means work and attack never fall below 75% , even if you are away all night. Tapping Wind adds 4% each tap. Winders hold it steady. About one wind-up in ten as a Winder is enough to keep the key at full. The Winding Touch research makes every gathering tap also wind the key, a quarter as much as a tap on the key itself. The key only starts to unwind once you research Swarm Drill, so the early game stays at full speed. Tip Active players tap Wind between other things. Idle players give about 10% of their wind-ups the Winder job and forget about it. Either is fine. Tapping Tapping gathers one resource at a time and stays useful all game thanks to a group of Tapping researches. Nimble Claws adds to each tap, Borrowed Hands makes a tap also gather a slice of what your workers bring in, Moth's Favour doubles taps on the resource where the moth has settled, and Overflowing Hands lets taps fill stores a little past their limit. Details are in Build and research . Helpers Later on the hive earns its own helpers, who do the busywork for you. See Helpers and automation . Previous How the climb works Next Build and research

Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The five pieces Tiers and patterns How your wind-ups look Expeditions Gearshards Your wind-ups are stronger the better they are equipped. Equipment lives in the Climb tab and is paid for in Springs. The five pieces Piece Gives, per wind-up and level First level costs Price grows Appears Mandibles +1 attack 12 Springs 33% Floor 1 Shells +8 health 10 Springs 33% Floor 1 Stingers +3 attack 60 Springs 35% Floor 2 Carapace +25 health 50 Springs 35% Floor 3 Wings +80 health 300 Springs 37% Floor 5 Each level adds to every wind-up in the swarm, so every level counts more the bigger the swarm. Tiers and patterns Every level of a piece costs more than the last. To make a piece much stronger, you need a pattern : a blueprint found in an expedition chamber. Applying a pattern lifts a piece to the next tier : Each tier multiplies the piece's per-level stats by 2.3 . Each tier multiplies its prices by 3 . The piece's levels restart at zero. Tier II is the first lift. The chamber that holds a pattern is at a fixed level for each piece: ten floors per tier. Piece Tier II Tier III Tier IV Tier V Mandibles Level 10 Level 20 Level 30 Level 40 Shells Level 10 Level 20 Level 30 Level 40 Stingers Level 11 Level 21 Level 31 Level 41 Carapace Level 12 Level 22 Level 32 Level 42 Wings Level 14 Level 24 Level 34 Level 44 The Climb tab always shows which chamber holds the next pattern for you. A chamber can only go as high as the floor you have already reached. How your wind-ups look The portrait on the Climb tab shows how far the hive's equipment has come. The look follows the tier of your equipment rather than its levels: Look How it arrives Newly made The starting look Armed Lift Mandibles to tier II with an expedition pattern Armoured Lift the Carapace to tier IV Winged Lift Wings to tier VII Veteran A Harness brings the last look (see The Grand Winding ) Armed: mandibles and a stinger, with a few scuffs. Armoured: layered shell plates and a sturdy carapace. Winged: delicate glass-and-brass wings. Veteran: an ornate harness over its armour, a soft glow around the key. Expeditions Expeditions are side chambers, available once you have reached floor 10 and researched Expedition Charts . You choose a chamber level in the Climb tab and pay Gearshards to enter. A chamber has 20 cogs of Rust. The first chamber, at level 10, costs 100 Gearshards. Each level above that costs 15% more. Chambers go only as high as the floor you have reached. Clearing one pays about ten minutes of the hive's gathering, a good way to top up supplies. It fills your stores but never goes past their limit. Your place in the tower is kept while you are in a chamber, and you return to it afterwards. Chambers hold patterns , and, very rarely, a curio . Approximate Gearshard prices: level 10 costs 100; level 20 about 400; level 30 about 1,600; level 40 about 6,600; level 50 about 27,000. Gearshards Gearshards cannot be gathered by a job. They drop: from Gatekeepers , about 15% of what a chamber at that floor costs, and never less than 1.5 times the floor number; from the Rust on every tenth cog , a smaller drop. x: Home Hivewright Guides Salvage Salvage Every tenth floor the Gatekeeper leaves three finds, and you keep one for the rest of the run. Updated 11 November 2026 Salvage is the hive's small roguelite layer. Every tenth floor, the Gatekeeper leaves three finds. You keep one . It changes the current run only and ends at your next Rewind . Every card makes one thing better and another worse, and none is strictly best, so the right pick depends on what is holding your run back. The first Salvage choice arrives at floor 10. In the Climb tab you see the three cards on offer and pick one. All the Salvage cards Card Effect Oil Surge +30% Oil, but the Hatchery works 10% slower Brass Rush +30% Brass, but 10% fewer Springs Keen Draughts +40% Schematics, but 10% less Oil Coil Cache +30% Springs, but 10% less Brass Wide Combs +15% housing, but assembly is 15% slower Quick Hatch +25% assembly speed, but each wind-up needs 50% more Oil Taut Springs Swarms strike 25% harder, but have 15% less health Hardened Shells Swarms have 30% more health, but strike 10% softer Swarm Tactics Swarms are 20% larger, but the key unwinds 25% faster Steady Key The key unwinds 40% slower, but floors pay 20% less Gearshard Hoard Gatekeepers drop double Gearshards, but floors pay 20% less Scout's Map Expeditions cost 40% fewer Gearshards, but pay 25% less Treasure Seekers Expeditions pay double, but cost 30% more Gearshards Long Shelves +30% storage, but Oil, Brass and Springs are gathered 10% slower Quick Strikes Swarms strike 20% more often, but have 15% less health Cheap Tools Equipment costs 25% fewer Springs, but swarms are 10% smaller Lucky Dust Chambers are twice as likely to hold a curio, but cost 30% more Gearshards Night Shift The hive works 50% longer while you are away, but the key unwinds 20% faster Brass Bones Swarms have 20% more health and you gather 10% more Brass, but 15% less Oil Hungry Hatchery +50% assembly speed, but 10% less housing Glass Mandibles Swarms strike 50% harder, but have 30% less health Three further cards, Deep Combs , Overwound Key and Patient Stores , are left only by the Gatekeepers of later Eras; see The Grand Winding . Choosing well Stuck on a wall? Look at what limits you. If swarms fall slowly but surely, a health card such as Hardened Shells may beat an attack card. If they win but slowly, think about strike speed. Hungry for Springs or Gearshards? Coil Cache and Gearshard Hoard fit a run that is waiting on equipment or patterns. Going away for a while? Night Shift stretches the time away that your hive works. See Offline progress and optional boosts . Hunting curios? Lucky Dust doubles the chance a chamber holds one. See Curios . Tip Salvage resets with every Rewind, so a card that makes a long, hard run easier is fine even if it makes the next one worse. You can choose again at floor 10, 20 and onwards. Some Trials remove Salvage altogether: see Trials . Previous Equipment and expeditions Next Tips for fast progress

s: Practical habits for early runs, stalls, Rewinds and long idle stretches.
x: Home Hivewright Guides Tips for fast progress Tips for fast progress Practical habits for early runs, stalls, Rewinds and long idle stretches. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page In your first run Keep the key wound When a swarm keeps falling Rewinding well Idle well Taps stay useful In your first run Follow the moth's goals in order. They are written so each one unlocks the next thing you need. See Getting started . Put every wind-up to work. An idle wind-up gathers nothing (although each idle one speeds up the Hatchery a little). Keep homes ahead of the Hatchery. The hive says when it is full. Raise storage the moment a store fills. A full store stops gathering. See Build and research . Start the Climb early. Researching Swarm Drill costs only 40 Schematics, and floors 1 to 5 are eased for new players. Keep the key wound The key sets work and attack between 75% and 100%. Tap Wind when you check in, or give about one in ten wind-ups the Winder job. See Wind-ups, jobs and the great key . When a swarm keeps falling Level your cheapest equipment first. Each level adds to every wind-up in the swarm. Research Formation Drills for bigger swarms, and build a Proving Ground once floor 4 opens it. Raise Hatchery speed so a fallen swarm returns quickly. Pick a Salvage card that covers your weak side, such as health if swarms die fast. See Salvage . Chase expedition patterns : a tier is a x2.3 jump in a piece's strength. See Equipment and expeditions . If you have reached floor 20, think about a Rewind . Rewinding well Do not Rewind the moment you can. Aether grows 9% for each extra floor after 20, so a few more floors are worth a great deal. A good time to Rewind is when the next floors are taking much longer than the last ones. Use the Aether preview. The Rewind tab tells you how many perk levels the Aether would buy. Start with Deft Gathering and Sharp Swarm , the cheapest perks. Add Warm Hatchery and Head Start as runs get longer. Try a Trial early. After two Rewinds, a Trial's permanent Aether bonus pays back every later Rewind. Silent Key unlocks the Taut Key perk. See Trials . Idle well Let helpers do the chores. Climb to floors 15, 30, 40, 50 and 70 to earn them. See Helpers and automation . Research Standing Orders at floor 30 so idle wind-ups take jobs for you. Buy Long Rest if you leave the hive for long stretches, or take the Night Shift Salvage when you know you are heading away. Save Time Jumps for a stall. A jump is worked out like time away, so it is worth more the stronger your hive is. See Offline progress and optional boosts . Taps stay useful Tapping research (Nimble Claws, Borrowed Hands, Moth's Favour, Overflowing Hands and Winding Touch) keeps manual play worthwhile. Tap the resource where the lantern moth has settled for the most. Tip If a run goes badly after your first Rewind, you can start it over for nothing before reaching floor 20. Perks and records are kept. Previous Salvage Next Rewind and perks

s: Wind time back from floor 20, keep your Aether, and spend it on permanent perks so every run climbs further.
x: Home Hivewright Systems Rewind and perks Rewind and perks Wind time back from floor 20, keep your Aether, and spend it on permanent perks so every run climbs further. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page What resets and what stays How much Aether? Perks Which perks first? Trials and the Rewind Looking ahead The Rewind: the hands spin back, the hive dissolves, and the moth watches calmly from the centre. A Rewind starts the hive again in exchange for Aether . It is the game's main loop: climb, Rewind, spend Aether on perks, and climb further next time. You can Rewind from floor 20 . What resets and what stays Resets Stays Resources, buildings, jobs and research Aether Wind-ups and equipment, including patterns Perks The tower: you start again on floor 1 Trial rewards and your records This run's Salvage Curios, helpers, the Loft and the moth Standing Orders, if you have researched it, starts each run already learned. The Rewind tab spells out what resets and what you keep before you confirm. The Rewind tab shows exactly what you will get before you confirm: Rewinding now gives X Aether. Each floor past 20 is worth more. It also shows what the Aether would buy. How much Aether? Aether grows with every floor you reach from floor 20, and each floor is worth 9% more than the one before it. On top of that you earn one Aether for each factor of ten of resources the run gathered. Trial bonuses, curios and the Loft multiply the total. From floors alone (before those multipliers), a Rewind pays roughly: Floor reached Aether from floors 20 4 25 30 30 70 40 227 50 598 60 1,477 80 8,483 100 47,749 The curve is steep, so a few extra floors are worth more than the same time spent Rewinding early. Tip Rewind when the next floors are slow. If you can still clear floors quickly, keep going; if the walls are taking an hour a floor, a Rewind and a handful of perks will carry you past them. Your tab shows how many perk levels the Aether would buy. After your first Rewind, a run that has not yet reached floor 20 can be started over for nothing, with all perks, Trials, curios and records kept. Perks Perks are permanent upgrades bought with Aether in the Rewind tab. Each level multiplies its effect, and each level costs more than the last. The price is the first-level cost multiplied by the growth factor for every level you already own. Perk Effect per level Max level First cost Cost grows by Deft Gathering x1.2 to everything wind-ups gather 200 3 27% Sharp Swarm x1.2 swarm attack 200 3 27% Tough Shells x1.1 swarm health 200 3 27% Warm Hatchery x1.2 assembly speed 100 4 37% Deep Stores +25% Oil, Brass and Springs storage 50 4 40% Head Start Each run starts with 2 more Cells and 50 more Oil and Brass 10 6 60% Long Rest The hive keeps working 1 more hour while you are away 8 5 50% Taut Key The key rests 5% tighter: about +2.5% work and attack even when you are away 5 8 60% Taut Key is locked until you complete the Silent Key Trial . Which perks first? Deft Gathering and Sharp Swarm are cheap and compound quickly. They carry most early Rewinds. Tough Shells helps when swarms fall on the way up. Warm Hatchery makes fallen swarms return sooner. Head Start makes the first minutes after every Rewind faster. It pays off the more you Rewind. Long Rest pays off if you leave the hive for long stretches. Trials and the Rewind After two Rewinds the Rewind tab opens Trials : challenge runs that bend one rule. A Trial starts with your next Rewind. Completing one permanently

s: Optional challenge runs that bend one rule of the hive, with stars to earn and permanent Aether bonuses.
x: Home Hivewright Systems Trials Trials Optional challenge runs that bend one rule of the hive, with stars to earn and permanent Aether bonuses. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page How they work Stars The Trials Rewards Tips for Trials A Trial is a challenge run. It bends one rule of the hive until you reach its target floor, and in return it permanently increases the Aether every Rewind pays. Trials are entirely optional and cost nothing to try. How they work Trials open after two Rewinds . In the Rewind tab, open Trials and choose one. It begins with your next Rewind . Climb to the Trial's target floor while its rule holds. The Trials window shows the rule again whenever you need it. Reaching the target gives you the Trial's reward at once and lifts the rule. You can leave a Trial early. Its rule lifts, but you lose its reward. Stars Every Trial can be completed three times for three stars. First star: reach the target floor. The rule lifts straight away, as it always has. Second and third stars: replay the Trial. This time the rule holds on until the third star. The second star is half as far again as the target, and the third is twice the target. Each new star stores a Time Jump : 15 minutes for the first star, 30 for the second and 60 for the third. See Offline progress and optional boosts . Stars 2 and 3 raise the Trial's Aether bonus to 125% and 150% of its first value. Stars are kept through Rewinds. They are lost at the Grand Winding, with the rest of your run's progress. The Trials Trial The rule Stars at floor No Wings Wings cannot be levelled or patterned 25 / 38 / 50 Rust Tide Rust creatures heal 3% of their health every second 20 / 30 / 40 Lean Hive Housing is halved 20 / 30 / 40 Silent Key The great key cannot be wound by hand 25 / 38 / 50 Shattered Drafts Gatekeepers offer no Salvage 30 / 45 / 60 Heavy Rust Rust creatures strike 50% harder 30 / 45 / 60 Dark Hive The lantern moth gives no light 35 / 52 / 70 Thin Oil Buildings cost twice the Oil 25 / 38 / 50 Dear Brass Buildings cost twice the Brass 25 / 38 / 50 Weary Wind-ups Wind-ups gather at half speed 30 / 45 / 60 Brittle Shells Swarm health is halved 30 / 45 / 60 Dull Stingers Swarm attack is halved 30 / 45 / 60 Iron Gatekeepers Gatekeepers have twice the health 35 / 52 / 70 A few more Trials open in later Eras; see The Grand Winding . Rewards Each Trial adds to the Aether multiplier on every Rewind. At the first star: Aether bonus Trials +20% Rust Tide +15% No Wings, Lean Hive, Shattered Drafts, Heavy Rust +10% Silent Key, Dark Hive, Thin Oil, Dear Brass, Weary Wind-ups, Brittle Shells, Dull Stingers, Iron Gatekeepers Bonuses add together. Completing all thirteen of these Trials once would more than double the Aether of every Rewind. Silent Key also unlocks the Taut Key perk. Tips for Trials Silent Key is a good first choice. Give some wind-ups the Winder job and you barely notice the rule, and it unlocks a perk. Dark Hive removes the moth's boost, so research and perks matter more. Trial runs do not get the "way back up" easing that makes already-climbed floors quick, so expect the early floors to take longer than in a normal run. Tip If a Trial is not going well, abandon it and take a normal Rewind. You lose nothing you already had. Previous Rewind and perks Next The lantern moth

s: A moth of living light that settles on the busiest part of your hive and makes it work faster.
x: Home Hivewright Systems The lantern moth The lantern moth A moth of living light that settles on the busiest part of your hive and makes it work faster. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page What it does The moth chooses, not you It grows with the tower Helping the moth along What it never does Where the moth comes from The moth arrives: a creature of light in a dark workshop at the tower's base. A lantern moth made of living light lives with the hive from the very first minute. It gives you the opening goals and later boosts whatever part of the hive it settles on. What it does Every 40 to 150 seconds , at random, the moth flits to another busy part of the hive and settles there. Its light boosts that one thing by 30% . The places it can settle are: the Hatchery , while it is assembling wind-ups, Oil , Brass , Springs or Schematics gathering, where you have workers on that job, the swarm , while it is out fighting, the great key , where its light slows the key's unwinding. The moth never settles on something idle, and it always chooses somewhere new if it has a choice. The Jobs and Climb tabs say where the moth is: The lantern moth has settled on the swarm, +30% . The moth chooses, not you You cannot steer the moth, so being away never wastes it. It uses the same randomness whether you watch or not, so time away plays out exactly as time watched. It grows with the tower Every time you restart a great clock , the moth glows brighter. Its bonus is 30% plus 10% for each great clock restarted in the current Era. The first great clock is at floor 100, so past floor 100 the moth gives 40%, past floor 200, 50%, and so on. Helping the moth along Moth's Favour research (see Build and research ): a tap on the resource where the moth has settled gathers double, and one more time for each further level. The Cracked lamp glass curio strengthens the moth's light. The Dark Hive Trial takes the moth's light away for a run. What it never does The moth cannot be bought, fed or upgraded with money, and being away does not harm it. It stays with the hive through every Rewind and the Grand Winding, and it works the same when the game is closed. Tip Because the moth boosts whatever it rests on, a hive with a little of everything benefits most: Oilers, Braziers, Coilers and Draughtsmen all give it somewhere to go, and a fighting swarm and a working Hatchery give it more. Where the moth comes from In the story it flies ahead of the swarm, rests on the stair rail and, at every great clock, flies into the light and comes back brighter than before. s: Five helpers you earn by climbing, each one a switch that takes over a chore while you play.
x: Home Hivewright Systems Helpers and automation Helpers and automation Five helpers you earn by climbing, each one a switch that takes over a chore while you play. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The five helpers Good to know Curio hunt Using helpers well As the hive climbs it earns helpers : small automatic hands that take over the busywork. Each helper is earned once, by reaching its floor in any Era, and is kept for good through every Rewind and the Grand Winding. They cost nothing to run. Every helper is a switch . Let it run, or turn it off and do it all by hand. The five helpers Helper Earned at floor What it does Store-keeper 15 Builds a Cistern, Bin or Rack when that store is 90% full Comb-builder 30 Builds the housing that gives the most room for its price, when it costs under a quarter of what you hold Archivist 40 Studies the cheapest research when it costs under a quarter of your Schematics Chart-reader 50 Sends the swarm into the chamber that holds your next pattern while you climb, when you have the Gearshards Pattern-fitter 70 Applies a found pattern and levels the piece back up, once your Springs can make it at least as strong as before Good to know Helpers only work while the game is open. During time away or a skip, they wait. That way you do not come back to stores that were spent as they filled. They never spend what a gift gave you. A resource held over its storage limit, such as from a gift pack, is left alone. Helpers and research are separate. Helpers are earned once for good; Standing Orders and Self-fitting Equipment are researches bought again each run (Standing Orders stays learned once you have it). See Build and research . Curio hunt The Chart-reader has an extra switch of its own: Curio hunt . With it on, the Chart-reader waits until your swarm has gone a minute without clearing a cog, then runs the highest chamber your Gearshards can pay for that is at least two levels below your wall. Easier chambers can still hold curios, and a hunt chamber that stalls too is left. Chambers 20 or more levels below hold no curios, so below that it waits. It is a hands-off way to look for curios when the climb has stalled. Using helpers well With the Store-keeper on, you rarely need to watch storage. The Comb-builder and Archivist buy things only when the price is under a quarter of what you hold. The Pattern-fitter saves the tapping needed to level a piece back up after every pattern. Tip Turn a helper off when you are saving up for something specific and flip it back on afterwards. Previous The lantern moth Next Offline progress and optional boosts

s: How the hive works while you are away, and a guide to the optional ad-supported boosts, the Lantern Pass and the rest of the free rewards.
x: Home Hivewright Systems Offline progress and optional boosts Offline progress and optional boosts How the hive works while you are away, and a guide to the optional ad-supported boosts, the Lantern Pass and the rest of the free rewards. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page When you are away Optional boosts The Lantern Pass Free rewards Time Jumps The shop's other items Hivewright is free to play and made to be played offline. You do not need an account or an internet connection. When you are away Your hive keeps working while the game is closed. Wind-ups keep gathering, the Hatchery keeps assembling, and swarms keep climbing. The great key rests half wound at worst, so work and attack never fall below 75% while you are away. Away time counts for up to 8 hours at once. The Long Rest perk adds one hour per level. Some Salvage and curios stretch it further. When you return, a welcome-back summary shows what the hive earned. Helpers wait until you are back; see Helpers and automation . Standing Orders lets idle wind-ups take jobs by themselves, so the hive grows while you are away. Optional boosts Hivewright shows some ads, but only optional ones: you choose each one, and each pays you something. No ad ever interrupts play by itself. The game's boost offers are never made in your first half hour of play, never in the first few minutes of a sitting, and appear at most once every half hour. If you tap Not now , the wait before the next offer doubles, up to four hours. Boost What a watched video gives Lantern Glow Half an hour of doubled gathering and hatching. You can bank up to four hours Free build Build a building you cannot yet afford, up to three an hour Welcome-back double Doubles what the hive gathered while you were away, once per return Rewind double Doubles the Aether of one Rewind Rally the swarm After a swarm has fallen five times on the same level, the next swarm and every swarm sent to that level after it fights at double attack and health until the level is cleared. At most three an hour Time Jump Stores a small jump of 10 to 30 minutes, up to three a day. Longer the further the hive has come Task swap Swap one of your daily tasks for another The Lantern Pass The Lantern Pass is a one-time purchase in the Shop. It removes the ads and lets you take every boost above without watching a video . The Pass is kept through every Rewind and Era. Everything else in the game works exactly the same without it, and the hive never needs it to progress. Free rewards First-week gifts. On each of your first seven days of returning to the hive, you get a gift of progress: 3, 4, 4, 6, 6, 8 and 12 hours of the hive's work. If you miss a day, the gifts wait for you. Daily tasks. Three small tasks a day, drawn fresh at your local midnight. They open with the Climb and are sized for a few minutes of normal play. Finish all three to open the daily chest, which holds a Time Jump and a pack of resources. Three chests in a week add a small bonus. A missed day costs you nothing. Hive Season. A new Season starts every eight weeks, with thirty tiers on a free reward track. You earn Season progress by playing: 10 for each floor cleared, 50 for a Rewind, 200 for an Era, plus a little for each opening goal. Every 250 points is a tier. Free rewards alternate between half an hour of Lantern Glow and 15 minutes of progress at once. Nothing counts down, and progress and rewards stay claimable after a Season ends. s: How tough the Rust gets floor by floor, what it is called and what each floor pays.
x: Home Hivewright Reference Floors and the Rust Floors and the Rust How tough the Rust gets floor by floor, what it is called and what each floor pays. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The Rust creatures How the numbers grow What each floor pays Drops Landmarks at a glance Looking up the tower: warm, lived-in floors below, rust and creeping shadows above. The Rust gets thicker the higher you climb, a flaky orange-brown scale over the brass, with creatures hiding in the shadows. The Rust creatures Ordinary Rust creatures come in seven kinds, and the kind you meet depends on the floor and cog: Rust mite Flake crawler Scale beetle Burr spider Verdigris slug Pitted wasp Corroded weevil They all use the same stats for a given floor and cog. The name is only for flavour. The last cog of each floor holds the Gatekeeper , see Gatekeepers and landmarks . How the numbers grow The Rust on the first cog of each floor has these base stats: Floor Rust health Rust attack 1 130 8 5 about 370 about 21 10 about 1,400 about 69 20 about 19,000 about 750 30 about 260,000 about 8,200 40 about 3.6 million about 89,000 50 about 50 million about 980,000 The rules behind the table: Health grows 30% per floor. Attack grows 27% per floor . Each cog on a floor is a little tougher than the last: +2% per cog , so the 49th cog is nearly double the first. The first five floors are eased to help new players: the Rust on floors 1 to 5 has 50%, 60%, 70%, 80% and 90% of its normal health. The Gatekeepers of floors 1 to 4 are also lighter. A chamber of a given level uses the Rust stats of that floor level. Floors you have already climbed are remembered. Floors more than ten below your best in the current Era are weaker, the further down the easier, so the early part of every run after a Rewind is quick. Your swarm grows faster than this early on, then you hit walls. See Tips for fast progress . What each floor pays Clearing a floor pays about a minute of your hive's gathering , with a minimum of 15 times the floor number in each resource. The Music-box comb curio and some Salvage choices raise or lower floor rewards. Drops Gearshards come from the Gatekeeper of every floor and from the Rust on every tenth cog. Salvage comes from the Gatekeeper of every tenth floor. See Salvage . Story fragments are told on each landmark floor. Landmarks at a glance Floor What opens or happens 1 First Gatekeeper 2 Tuners and Stingers 3 Formation Drills and the Carapace 4 Proving Ground 5 Wings, Hoardcomb, and a first-run gift 10 First story fragment, first Salvage choice, expeditions 15 Store-keeper helper, a first-run gift 20 Rewind 30 Comb-builder helper, Standing Orders 40 Archivist helper, Spire 50 Chart-reader helper, Escapement Hall 60 Self-fitting Equipment 70 Pattern-fitter helper 100 The first great clock For what lies beyond, see the spoiler pages on Gatekeepers and landmarks . s: The guardian on every floor's last cog, the landmark floors every ten, the great clocks and the story the tower tells.
x: Home Hivewright Reference Gatekeepers and landmarks Gatekeepers and landmarks The guardian on every floor's last cog, the landmark floors every ten, the great clocks and the story the tower tells. Updated 11 November 2026 Spoilers ahead. This page discusses story events and reveals. Come back after you have played if you want to find things out yourself. On this page The Gatekeeper Landmark floors Later Eras The great clocks The story so far Tips for the climb Warning This page describes the story fragments and later parts of the tower. Skip it if you want to find them yourself. The tower relit: every window glowing, the rust falling away like autumn leaves. The Gatekeeper The last cog of every floor is held by a Gatekeeper . Compared with the Rust on the same floor's other cogs, a Gatekeeper: has five times the health of an ordinary cog on that floor (three times on floors 1 to 4, to be gentle with new players), strikes 50% harder , drops Gearshards , the currency for expeditions. Beating it clears the floor. A swarm that falls to a Gatekeeper keeps the floor it reached; it tries again. Landmark floors Every tenth floor is a landmark . Its Gatekeeper leaves three Salvage finds (keep one; see Salvage ), and the hive hears a story fragment. Landmarks are also where new parts of the game tend to open: floor 10 opens expeditions, floor 20 the Rewind. Later Eras After the Grand Winding, landmark Gatekeepers learn tricks. One new ability is added for each Era past the first, in this order: Ability What the Gatekeeper does Mending Heals a little every second Plated Every strike does a quarter less Twinned Has twice the health Furious Strikes half as hard again once below half health The Rust itself also gets a new name in each Era: Tarnished, Gilt-rot, Glassbound, Starved. See The Grand Winding . The great clocks Every 100 floors , a great clock is restarted. The gears catch, the pendulum swings and bells ring down the whole tower, and warm light runs along every stair you have climbed. The moth flies into the light and comes back brighter, and each great clock strengthens the lantern moth . The tower does not end at the clock, and the climb continues above it. The story so far The tower's story is told in fragments, one on each landmark floor. They come in arcs of ten , one arc per great clock. Ten arcs are written, which carries the story to floor 1,000, and short echo lines cover the floors beyond. Arc one, floors 10 to 100. A moth flies ahead of the swarm. On the wall, someone has made small neat tally marks in rows of twelve, with a tiny key beside each row. The marks stop halfway on floor 20, the last drawn very lightly, as if whoever made it meant to come back. Further up the hive finds an open workshop, a bell that has never been rung, a note folded under a step ("Thank you for coming up the stair"), a mural of brass insects and a moth of light, and Rust that pulls back from the ticking of the swarm. Around floor 90 a vast pendulum comes into view, hanging still in the dark far above, and the moth flies up towards it further than it has ever gone. Arc two, 110 to 200. The wrights who built the tower: bunks made up neatly, one carved with the name Ottilie, a sealed letter addressed to "the keeper beyond the wall", Rust grown into silent flowers, a brass map of the tower that does not end, and a faint ticking from somewhere above that is not your own. x: Home Hivewright Reference Curios Curios Twelve rare treasures found in expedition chambers, kept for good through every Rewind and Era. Updated 11 November 2026 Spoilers ahead. This page discusses story events and reveals. Come back after you have played if you want to find things out yourself. On this page All twelve Duplicates The odds Hunting curios Warning This page lists every curio, including the rare ones. Ottilie's lamp, one of the four rare curios: an old brass lantern with a tiny key engraved on its side. A curio is a small wright-made treasure found, very rarely, in an expedition chamber. Once found, it is kept for good : through every Rewind and even through the Grand Winding. Each gives a permanent boost. There are twelve curios: eight common and four rare. The collection is shown in the Journal tab. All twelve Curio Boost (first copy) Rarity Ottilie's thimble +10% to everything wind-ups gather Common Wright's whetstone +10% swarm attack Common Patched shell plate +10% swarm health Common Spare mainspring +10% Hatchery speed Common Cracked lamp glass +10% to the lantern moth's light Common Folded map scrap Chambers cost 10% fewer Gearshards Common Brass tally stick +10% Aether from Rewinds Common Wax-sealed oilcan +10% Oil, Brass and Springs storage Common Pendulum bob +5% how often swarms strike Rare Keeper's key ring +10% Gearshard drops Rare Music-box comb +10% what floors pay Rare Ottilie's lamp +10% time the hive works while you are away Rare Duplicates Finding a curio you already have makes it 15% stronger , and the boost compounds. A +10% curio becomes +11.5% with a second copy, then about +13.2% with a third. The odds Curios are rare. A cleared chamber at your current floor has a 0.8% chance of holding one. For every level the chamber is below your floor, the chance falls by 0.04 percentage points, and chambers 20 or more levels below your floor hold none. From chamber level 40 , one find in five is a rare curio, so the four rare ones come only from high chambers. High chambers are worth their extra Gearshards, and the best hunting ground is just below the wall you are on. Chamber level relative to your floor Chance of a curio At your floor 0.8% 5 below 0.6% 10 below 0.4% 15 below 0.2% 20 or more below None Hunting curios Lucky Dust Salvage doubles the chance, at the price of more Gearshards. Curio hunt (a switch on the Chart-reader helper) runs suitable chambers automatically when your climb has stalled. See Helpers and automation . The Keeper's key ring and Folded map scrap curios themselves make Gearshards go further, which helps with the hunt. Note The Achievements "A curious find", "Collector" and "Cabinet of curios" are for finding your first curio, six different curios and all twelve. They are through Google Play Games and entirely optional. See Equipment and expeditions for how chambers work. Previous Gatekeepers and landmarks Next The Loft

s: A second layer above the hive where you share the great key's spare winding among six gear trains that level up by themselves.
x: Home Hivewright Reference The Loft The Loft A second layer above the hive where you share the great key's spare winding among six gear trains that level up by themselves. Updated 11 November 2026 Spoilers ahead. This page discusses story events and reveals. Come back after you have played if you want to find things out yourself. On this page The six trains Torque and power How it fits with everything else Warning The Loft opens at floor 60. This page describes it in full. Above the hive, a loft opens once you have reached floor 60 in any Era. In the Loft, the great key's spare winding is stored as Torque . You share that Torque out among six gear trains . Each train turns by itself, slowly, even while you are away. Every time one comes all the way round, it gains a level : a small, lasting boost to part of the hive. Later levels take longer. Aether has a second use here besides perks: it buys more Torque and more power. The six trains Train Boosts Per level Gathering Train Everything wind-ups gather +1% Hatching Train Hatchery speed +1% Striking Train Swarm attack +1% Plating Train Swarm health +1% Aether Train Aether from Rewinds +0.5% Shard Train Gearshard drops +1% Each level compounds on the last, like perks. Torque and power You start with 10 Torque to share. Each capacity upgrade, bought with Aether, adds 5 more. Each train turns at a rate set by the Torque on it, times your power . Each power upgrade, bought with Aether, multiplies the speed by 1.25. The first level of a train takes 5,000 Torque-seconds. Each later level needs 35% more than the one before. Capacity costs 100 Aether for the first upgrade and rises 60% each time; power costs 150 and rises 80% each time. Share evenly splits all your Torque between the six trains in one tap. Tip Torque on a train is not spent: you can move it from one train to another whenever you like. Put it on Aether before a Rewind you are about to do, and on Gathering or Striking while you push through a wall. How it fits with everything else The Loft is kept through Rewinds, like perks. It starts again at the Grand Winding , with perks and Aether. Trains turn while you are away like everything else, and a long absence can bring several levels at once. Read about the deeper reset on The Grand Winding , and about the permanent boosts you earn along the way in Rewind and perks . Previous Curios Next The Grand Winding and Eras

x: Home Hivewright Reference The Grand Winding and Eras The Grand Winding and Eras The deepest reset, which starts a new Era with richer rewards, a tougher tower, a new Harness and a new colour for the hive. Updated 11 November 2026 Spoilers ahead. This page discusses story events and reveals. Come back after you have played if you want to find things out yourself. On this page What an Era is What resets What stays What you gain What gets harder The Harness Era-only Trials and Salvage Achievements Should I do it? Warning This page describes the late game in full. The Grand Winding is a deeper reset above the Rewind. It opens when you restart the first great clock by climbing past floor 100 . It is optional, and it is always previewed: the confirmation screen lists exactly what resets, what stays and what you gain before you commit. What an Era is The game counts Eras . Your first playthrough is Era I. Each Grand Winding begins the next Era: II, III, IV and so on, without end. The Grand Winding opens again at higher floors as you go. You must climb past 100 floors in Era I, 200 in Era II, 300 in Era III , and so on. Each Era asks for 100 more floors than the last. A new Era: the tower wakes and the Rust falls away like autumn leaves. What resets Everything earned in play: all resources, Aether and every perk , buildings, jobs, research, equipment, expeditions, Salvage, Trial progress and stars, your floor, and the Loft. What stays Curios , which are kept for good. The lantern moth . Helpers , which are earned for good. Your Era count and every theme you have unlocked . Time Jumps in your stored pile. Records : the game keeps your best floor in every Era, shown in the Journal. Anything you bought in the Shop, and your achievements. What you gain A permanent Era reward : everything wind-ups gather, and your Aether gains, are multiplied by 2 for each Era . Era II is x2, Era III x4, Era IV x8. A theme for the hive. Each Era unlocks a new metal for the tower and the hive. Era II unlocks Silverwork , then Goldwork , Obsidian and Starlight . They are earned only by playing. Once unlocked, a theme can be used in any Era. A new Harness (see below). A new opening line as the tower wakes. Era II begins: "Silver light runs down the stair. Somewhere above, a second great clock is waiting to be found." What gets harder Each Era raises: Rust and Gatekeeper health and attack: x3 per Era. Era II is x3, Era III x9, Era IV x27. Building and equipment prices: x1.5 per Era. Landmark Gatekeepers gain one extra ability per Era : Mending, Plated, Twinned and Furious (see Gatekeepers and landmarks ). The Rust gets a new name: Tarnished , then Gilt-rot , Glassbound and Starved . Rewards double while the Rust triples, so the early floors go faster at first, then the walls arrive sooner. To get through them you need better perks, smarter Salvage and Trial rewards. The Harness Every Era past the first adds one Harness , named after its theme: Silverwork Harness in Era II, Goldwork Harness in Era III and so on. You keep the earlier ones. Each level of a Harness multiplies swarm attack and health by 1.06 . A Harness is paid for in Springs, starting at 50,000 for Era II's. Each later Era's Harness costs 50 times more, and climbs in price faster per level. It resets on a Rewind, so you build it up again each run. It is the growth that lets a later Era climb its extra hundred floors. Tip The game's own advice after a Grand Winding is to level the new Era's Harness in the Cl

s: Quick answers to the questions new players ask most about Hivewright.
x: Home Hivewright Reference FAQ FAQ Quick answers to the questions new players ask most about Hivewright. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page Basics The hive The climb Rewind and beyond Rewards and extras Basics Is Hivewright free? Yes. It is free to play, with optional rewarded videos and an optional shop. Everything that affects play can also be earned in the game, and there is no energy system. See Offline progress and optional boosts . Do I need an internet connection or an account? No. You can play offline with no account. Signing in to Google Play Games is optional and only adds leaderboards and achievements. Which languages does it support? English, Dutch, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Russian, Japanese, Korean and Chinese. Is there an energy system or daily-login pressure? No. Missing a day costs you nothing. Daily tasks and gifts wait for you. The hive Why is my hive not making new wind-ups? Check that you have a Hatchery, that you have enough Oil (each wind-up uses a little), and that you have room. If the hive says it is full, build more Cells or other housing. Why did my resource stop going up? Its store is full. Build an Oil Cistern, Brass Bin or Spring Rack, or spend some. See Build and research . Where are Gearshards gathered? They are not gathered by a job. They drop from Gatekeepers and from the Rust on every tenth cog. What is the great key and do I need to tap it? It is the hive's winding. A wound key makes work and attack faster, up to 100%. It never drops below 75%, even when you are away. Tap Wind , or put about one wind-up in ten on the Winder job. See Wind-ups, jobs and the great key . The climb My swarm keeps falling. What now? Level your equipment, wind the key, research Formation Drills, build a Proving Ground and look at Salvage. The full list is in Tips for fast progress . Does the swarm climb while I am away? Yes. The hive works and climbs while the game is closed, up to eight hours at a time, plus one more hour for every level of the Long Rest perk. What does Stop climbing do? It calls the swarm home at once. Survivors rejoin the Swarmers if there is room. Rewind and beyond When should I Rewind? You can from floor 20. Each floor above 20 pays 9% more Aether than the one before it, so a Rewind is best when climbing has slowed. See Rewind and perks . Will a Rewind delete my progress? It resets the run (resources, buildings, wind-ups, equipment and the tower) but keeps your Aether, perks, Trial rewards, records, curios, helpers and the lantern moth. What are Trials? Optional challenge runs that bend one rule. They open after two Rewinds and permanently raise Aether gains. See Trials . What is the Grand Winding? A deeper reset that opens after you restart the first great clock, with a new Era, bigger rewards and a tougher tower. It is explained, with spoilers, on The Grand Winding and Eras . Rewards and extras What does the Lantern Pass do? It removes the ads and lets you take every optional boost without watching a video. It is kept through every Rewind and Era. How do gift codes work? Type the code into the Shop. Capitals and dashes do not matter, and each code works once per hive. What are Achievements? Optional goals through Google Play Games, such as A hive wakes (assemble your first wind-up), The first lamp (reach floor 10), Wound back (your first Rewind) and Tried and tested (complete a Trial). Where can I ask a question or share feedback? The BlairsLab Discord. The invite link is inside

s: Every Hivewright term in one place, from Aether to Winders.
x: Home Hivewright Reference Glossary Glossary Every Hivewright term in one place, from Aether to Winders. Updated 11 November 2026 A quick reference to the words used in the game and on this wiki. Terms that belong to later parts of the game are marked. Term Meaning Aether The permanent currency you earn from a Rewind and spend on perks (and, later, the Loft). Archivist A helper that studies the cheapest research for you. Brass A resource gathered by Braziers; used for buildings. Brazier The job that gathers Brass. Cell, Comb, Gallery, Spire Housing buildings, holding 3, 7, 18 and 35 wind-ups. See Build and research . Chamber A side room, entered on an expedition, that holds patterns and, rarely, curios. Chart-reader A helper that runs expedition chambers for you. Cog One enemy position on a floor. A floor has 50. Coiler The job that gathers Springs. Curio A rare permanent treasure from a chamber. See Curios . Spoilers. Draughtsman The job that draws Schematics. Era A playthrough tier from the Grand Winding. See The Grand Winding . Spoilers. Expedition A run into a side chamber of 20 cogs, paid for with Gearshards. See Equipment and expeditions . Floor One level of the tower; 50 cogs, the last held by a Gatekeeper. Gatekeeper The tougher guardian on the last cog of each floor. See Gatekeepers and landmarks . Gearshards The currency for expeditions, dropped by Gatekeepers and the Rust. Grand Winding The deeper reset that begins a new Era. Spoilers. Great clock A clock restarted every 100 floors; each brightens the moth. Great key The hive's winding; its Tension scales work and attack. Harness Era equipment that multiplies swarm attack and health. Spoilers. Hatchery The building that assembles wind-ups. Helper An automatic hand earned by reaching a floor. See Helpers and automation . Landmark floor Every tenth floor, with a story fragment and Salvage. Lantern Glow A spell of doubled gathering and hatching, banked up to four hours. Lantern Pass An optional purchase that removes ads and takes the optional boosts without a video. Lantern moth The moth of light that boosts the busiest part of the hive. See The lantern moth . Loft A layer above the hive with six gear trains. See The Loft . Spoilers. Updated 16 November 2026 On this page Your corner of the world The lantern moth Resets with a reason The other games Hivewright happens in the Evenwold , the country every BlairsLab game is set in. You never need to know any of it to climb the tower. Your corner of the world The great clock tower is so tall its top is lost in cloud, and its clocks stopped one dawn. The hive of wind-ups climbs it floor by floor, restarting great clocks as it goes. The Rust gathers on floors where time has been left alone. Read more in Floors and the Rust . The lantern moth The lantern moth is the one creature that appears in every BlairsLab game. Here it settles on the busiest part of your hive and glows brighter at every great clock. Elsewhere it does different jobs, but it is never a weapon, is never sold, and is not harmed when you are away. Resets with a reason Every BlairsLab game has a reset with a reason in its story. In Hivewright it is the Rewind . In the other games it is a Fold, or a bell rung backwards. What you learned always stays learned. The other games The Last Second Workshop : a clockmaker's workshop in Meridia, a city held at the last second of the day. The Last Bell : tower defence in a valley where every clock has stopped but one bell. The Lamplighter : light the road and survive the Rust (in closed testing). The Belfry Gun : hold a hill town's wall, wave after wave (in testing). The Roads Between : a story of small towns and stopped clocks (in closed testing). No game rewards you for owning another. For the whole picture, start at the Evenwold . Previous Glossary

s: A hand-painted tower-defence game where you guard the last ringing bell and can ring it backwards to take the last minute again.
x: The valley at dusk: the bell tower on its hill, and a lantern moth keeping it company. Every clock in the valley has stopped except one, in a bell tower, and you are its keeper. The old workshops went quiet long ago and the wind-ups they made ran down where they stood. Now the Rust has got into their springs and they are waking up and walking the cobbled roads towards the one thing that still ticks. The sound of the bell draws them in. The Last Bell is a tower-defence game for your phone. You build towers on stone pads beside the roads and stop each wave of wind-ups before it reaches the bell. Every wind-up you stop is mended : the Rust falls away and the parts are yours to spend. Ringing the bell backwards Sooner or later a wave you didn't plan for slips through. In The Last Bell you ring the bell backwards and the last 30 seconds are undone. The field pauses and faint echoes show you where the wind-ups got through. Move a tower, sell one or build a new one, then play the minute again. The wind-ups arrive in the same order and the same way, and every replay makes your towers strike a little harder. The details are on the Rewind page. After a rewind: glowing trails show where wind-ups got through, and towers ringed in grey never struck. How a run goes Build. Tap a glowing pad and pick a tower. Your first Clapper costs 20 Parts. See How to play . Defend. A new wave walks in about every 30 seconds. Mended wind-ups drop Parts, which you spend on more towers and on upgrading the ones you have. Rewind. You start each run with one rewind charge. Recast. When the bell's mainspring runs down, the run melts into Bell-metal , which you spend in the Foundry so the next run goes further. Runs are short at first and get longer as you grow. The clock face on the bell tower moves one hour every ten waves, and at each hour a Warden arrives. At midnight the Toll comes. See The clock face . What is in the valley Dozens of towers in seven rarities, from the Clapper up to Tamsin Hale's own designs. Each tower chooses one of two final forms when fully upgraded. Clockwork wind-ups : Tickers, Scuttlers, armoured Platebacks, paper-winged Gliders, bolt-throwing Spinners, and more, each with one obvious counter. Valleys to defend : Wandering Roads, which change every run, nine hand-made valleys, and the Open Field where you build your own maze. Trials , a Daily Valley and a fortnightly Peal if you want a challenge. Research and time away : the tower holds while you are gone, so you never come back to a lost run. Tamsin and the moth The bell tower once belonged to Tamsin Hale , a bell-founder who kept it ringing alone for years and left her notebook in the belfry. The notebook is where you learn the bell can ring backwards. The story arrives in short pages as you reach milestones; see The story (spoilers). A small lantern moth lives in the belfry. s: The whole loop of The Last Bell in one page: build, defend, rewind, recast, improve.
x: Home The Last Bell Start here How to play How to play The whole loop of The Last Bell in one page: build, defend, rewind, recast, improve. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The screen Build Defend Rewind Recast Improve for good A run in progress: the bell tower in the centre, towers on stone pads, the next wave waiting underneath. The screen The field is a square with the bell tower in the middle, sized for a portrait phone. Roads run in from the edges to the bell. Along the top you see the wave number, the hour on the clock face, the mainspring (the bell tower's health) and your Parts . Beneath the field a strip shows the next wave: its wind-ups as small pictures with counts, a "new" mark the first time a kind appears, and the seconds until it arrives. At the bottom are Ring back 30 s , a speed button and Pause. Build Tap a glowing stone pad to choose a tower from the ring. Pads sit beside the roads and around the tower itself. You begin with eight pads , and the Foundry can add more. Each tower costs Parts. The Clapper, the usual first tower, costs 20, and you start a run with 45. Tap a tower you have built to upgrade it (a tower can be raised to level 10 within a run) or sell it. Each level makes a tower strike harder, but the next level costs more: each upgrade costs a little over one and a half times the one before. Selling returns 70 percent of what you spent. After a rewind, while the field is paused, selling returns everything. Defend A wave arrives about every 30 seconds, and the waves grow tougher. Wind-ups walk the road to the bell. Every one that reaches it takes some of the mainspring, though the bell tower strikes back weakly, so a few strays are never fatal. Every wind-up your towers stop is mended , and drops Parts. Call the next wave early. Once the current wave has finished arriving, a "Call now" button offers to bring the next wave immediately for bonus Parts: the more time you skip, the bigger the bonus. Calling early earns more, but there's no penalty for letting it play itself. Rewind You start with one rewind charge. When a wave goes wrong, tap Ring back 30 s . The whole story is on the Rewind page. Recast When the mainspring runs down, the run is over. You can also recast by choice from wave 20 onwards. Either way the run melts into Bell-metal : the further you got, and the more Wardens and Tolls you stopped, the more you receive. Parts, the towers on the field and the wave count are cleared. Bell-metal, tower unlocks, Foundry upgrades, research and the Roll of woken wind-ups are kept. Improve for good Spend Bell-metal in the Foundry on permanent upgrades and on tower stars, and start research . New towers and valleys open on their own as you reach further waves. The Foundry, early on: upgrades that strengthen every run, and the towers you have unlocked. Tip Build a second tower before you upgrade the first, save your rewind charge for a wave that surprises you, and keep an eye on the next-wave strip. Next Your first hour

Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The guided first run What to expect A good opening After the first run Your first towers. Three are ready at the start; the rest open as you reach further. The guided first run The very first run holds the first wave back until you have built a tower, and the lantern moth talks you through it: Tap a glowing stone pad beside the road. Choose the Clapper . It costs 20 Parts and strikes steadily. Mend a few wind-ups, then build a second tower on another pad. Tap a tower and choose the + to raise its level. Stronger towers hold later waves. You have one rewind charge, so save it. When a wind-up reaches the bell and the mainspring drops, tap Ring back 30 s . When the bell finally falls, recast it in the Foundry to grow stronger. What to expect You begin with three towers: the Clapper , the Spring-gun and the Chime post . The rest open as your best wave grows (details on Common towers ): Best wave reached New tower 8 Weight-drop 14 Tack-thrower 16 Kennel 20 Bellows 25 Damper 30 Catchwheel Your first Warden arrives at wave 10, a larger wind-up of the newest kind on the road. The wind-ups themselves come in this order: Tickers from the first wave, Scuttlers from wave 10, Platebacks from wave 20 and Gliders from wave 31. See The wind-ups . A good opening Two towers early beat one strong tower. Cover the road in two places before you upgrade. Mix a fast tower with a heavy one. The Spring-gun's quick light shots and the Weight-drop's slow crushing blows cover each other's gaps. Look at the strip under the field. A new kind of wind-up is marked "new" there, so you can plan for it. Spend as you go. Unspent Parts are lost when the run ends. After the first run When the mainspring runs down, recast. Open the Foundry and buy the cheap upgrades first. Spare Parts and Stronger mainspring help straight away, and More pads lets you build more. Then start another run. Each one should reach a little further, and after your third recast the Trials open. Towers unlock by the best wave you have ever reached, in any run, so even a run that ends badly can open something new. Tip The guided run suggests ringing back when a wind-up first reaches the bell. Do it, because the echoes show you how to read a failing wave. Next: Rewind or Towers . Previous How to play Next Rewind the minute

s: How the bell rings backwards: the 30-second window, echoes, Hindsight, charges and the bell that rewinds itself.
x: Home The Last Bell Systems Rewind the minute Rewind the minute How the bell rings backwards: the 30-second window, echoes, Hindsight, charges and the bell that rewinds itself. Updated 11 November 2026 On this page What happens when you ring back The minute plays the same way Hindsight Charges The bell keeps watch The moth remembers When to ring back The field after ringing back: trails glow where wind-ups reached the tower; towers ringed in grey never struck. Tamsin Hale's notebook says that if you ring the bell the wrong way it remembers the last minute and lets you have it again. It also says the bell tires, so you should let it gather itself between times. What happens when you ring back Tap Ring back 30 s . The last 30 seconds of the run are undone: wind-ups, Parts, towers and the mainspring all return to how they were half a minute ago. Then the field pauses , and the erased minute stays behind as faint echoes : Glowing trails show the paths of wind-ups that got through to the bell. Towers ringed in grey never struck anything in that minute. While the field is paused you may: Move towers, Sell towers for a full refund (outside a rewind, selling returns 70 percent), Build or upgrade with the Parts you had at that moment. When you are ready, tap Play the minute again . The minute plays the same way The wind-ups come in the same order and the same way. That flock of Gliders will come over the grass again, and that Plateback will be on the road again, so whatever you change is what makes the difference. Hindsight Each time you replay a stretch, your towers strike 10 percent harder until you pass the moment you rang back from, and this stacks up to +30 percent if you ring back repeatedly. So rewinding helps even if you change nothing, which is handy when you are playing hands-off. Charges Starting charges 1 Most the bell can hold 3 (with two Foundry upgrades) Recharge A charge comes back after 40 mends Faster recharge Foundry "Quick bell" takes 5 mends off per level; research "Swifter echoes" takes 2 off per level, down to a minimum of 10 Mends in a replayed minute are not counted twice, so you can't farm charges by rewinding. The Foundry's upgrade The bell remembers lets the bell hold one more charge, twice. See Recast, Foundry and stars for the costs. The bell keeps watch Another Foundry upgrade, The bell keeps watch , lets the bell act on its own: when the mainspring would run down and the bell has a charge, it rings back by itself and plays the minute again. It helps a lot when you leave a run playing. The moth remembers A rewind doesn't move the lantern moth . It stays exactly where it was. When to ring back Early is the cheapest time to learn. Your first rewind teaches you to read echoes. Save the charge for a wave you did not predict, such as the first Gliders, the first Warden of an hour or a Toll. Read the echoes. If trails cluster on one road, you don't have enough coverage there. If a tower is ringed in grey, move it. Chain rewinds when you have two or more charges: the Hindsight bonus stacks. Some Trials take the bell away completely or slow its recharge. See also Tips for deep waves . Note In the Story, the keeper rewinds at the bell tower because it is the last ticking clock in the valley. Previous Your first hour Next Recast, the Foundry and stars

Updated 11 November 2026 On this page Recast The Foundry What to buy first Stars Unlocks The Foundry after a first recast. The price of each upgrade is shown on its button. Recast A run ends when the bell tower's mainspring runs down. From wave 20 you may also recast by choice from the run screen. Either way, the run melts into Bell-metal : the further you got, the more you receive, and Wardens and Tolls stopped add a good bonus on top. The number is shown on the button ("Recast now +278") before you commit. Kept Cleared Bell-metal, tower unlocks, stars, Foundry upgrades, research, the Roll of woken wind-ups, story Parts, towers on the field, the wave count, this run's crew The best wave you reach also counts for good: it is what opens new towers, valleys and Trials. Tip If you've stalled, recast by choice from wave 20. A fresh run reaches the same waves faster with the Bell-metal you just gained. The Foundry Bell-metal buys permanent upgrades. Every price rises each time you buy that upgrade. Upgrade What it does Starting price Levels More pads One more stone pad to build on in every run 30 8 Spare Parts Start each run with 20 more Parts 12 15 Stronger mainspring The mainspring holds 15 percent more 18 12 Truer strikes Every tower strikes 15 percent harder 20 30 Scavenging 10 percent more Parts from every mend 20 20 The bell remembers The bell can hold one more rewind charge 140 2 Quick bell A rewind charge comes back 5 mends sooner 45 5 Crew quarters Start each run with one more crew from the Roll 300 3 The bell keeps watch When the mainspring would run down, the bell rings back by itself if it has a charge 250 1 A second bench Research two projects at once 400 1 Prices climb by a fixed share with each level: from about 38 percent more per level for Truer strikes, to 75 percent for More pads, and four times for The bell remembers. What to buy first Spare Parts and Stronger mainspring are cheap and help from the first wave. More pads gives you somewhere to build; you begin with eight. Truer strikes is the long-term workhorse: 30 levels of 15 percent. The bell remembers and The bell keeps watch make the Rewind much more forgiving. A second bench doubles your research . Stars Each tower you have unlocked can be given stars in the Foundry. A star makes that tower strike 25 percent harder in every later run (compounding), up to 15 stars. The first star costs 25 Bell-metal for a Common tower, and 40, 65, 100, 150, 225 or 300 for Uncommon, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic or Exalted. Each further star costs about 45 percent more than the last. Stars go on the tower itself, so both final forms benefit. Put them on the towers you actually build. Unlocks New towers and valleys open themselves as your best wave grows; the home screen shows the next one. See Towers and Valleys . At three recasts the Trials open. Note The Open Field, the Daily Valley and the Peal each have their own separate starting point, so their upgrades do not carry over to your main valley (and vice versa). See The Open Field and Daily Valley and the Peal . Previous Rewind the minute Next Research and time away

Updated 11 November 2026 On this page The tower holds Research Time skips Away earnings Daily tasks The tower holds while you are away: you never come back to a lost run. The tower holds When you leave the game, the wave doesn't move, so you never come back to a lost run. Research keeps going and Bell-metal trickles in. Research Open the Foundry, pick a project and pay its Bell-metal. It then takes real time (minutes at first, then hours) and keeps going whether the game is open or not. You have one bench, and the Foundry's A second bench gives you two. Project Effect per level Levels First level costs First level takes Finer springs Every tower strikes 6 percent harder 20 60 Bell-metal 5 min Quicker hands 8 percent more Parts from every mend 15 50 5 min Deeper spring The mainspring holds 10 percent more 15 40 4 min Swifter echoes A rewind charge comes back 2 mends sooner 6 120 15 min Longer reach Every tower reaches 3 percent further 8 150 20 min A patient bell Bell-metal gathers for one more hour while you are away 8 100 2 h Each level costs more and takes longer than the last: costs rise by 60 percent per level for the first three projects and by 90 to 120 percent for the last three, and times grow in a similar way. Finished research strengthens every run from the next one on. Time skips Some daily tasks and Trial stars give time skips : minutes taken off the project on a bench. If no project is running, the time waits in a bank (up to six hours) and is used on the next project you start. Away earnings While you are away (for at least five minutes), the bell gathers Bell-metal based on your best wave. It is about a tenth of what a full run to your best wave would melt into, for every hour you are away, for up to four hours . Each level of A patient bell adds one more hour to that cap. A welcome-back card shows what was gathered. Tip Start a long research project before bed and a short one before a walk. Daily tasks Each day brings three small tasks, such as "Reach wave 12 in one run", "Build five towers", "Call three waves early" or "Ring the bell back once". They scale with your best wave. Finishing them pays Bell-metal, a rewind charge for the next run or research time, and there is a daily chest as well. You get one free reroll a day, and a task that has become impossible can always be rerolled. See also Recast, Foundry and stars and Trials .
